verses.1: And Abraham was old in those days, but Jehovah blessed Abraham in everything.
verses.2: And Abraham said to his servant, “The old man who is the chief priest, please put your hand under my feet.”
verses.3: And I will make you a covenant with the LORD, the God of the heavens and the God of the earth. I will not take any wife from the daughters of the Canaanites who are my neighbors.
verses.4: For to my land and to my birthplace you will go, and you will take a wife for my son Isaac.
verses.5: And the servant said to him, “Do not let her go with you to that land. She should stay here and bring your son back to the land from which you came.”
verses.6: And Abraham said to him, “Be careful, for you will not be able to bring your son back to life.”
verses.7: Yehova, the God of heaven! You who took me from the house of my father and from the land where I was born. You who spoke to me and commanded me, saying, “To your descendants I will give this land.” He will send his messengers before you, so that you may take a wife from there for your son.
verses.8: And if a woman does not want to go with you, and I remove her from my place of rest, then only my children shall remain there.
verses.9: And the servant placed his hand under Abraham’s arm. He sat down with him regarding this matter.
verses.10: And the servant took twelve donkeys from his master’s stables. He carried all the goods of his master with him. Then he went to the city of Nahor.
verses.11: And the shepherds blessed them as they left the city, towards the river. This happened in the evening, when the shepherds were leaving.
verses.12: And the LORD, the God of Abraham, said to him, “Come before me today, and I will show you kindness and favor.”
verses.13: Look, I am standing on the shore of the sea, and the people of the city are coming out to swim in the water.
verses.14: And the young man who said to her, “Please, let me have it as well,” and she said, “Yes, I will give you your clothes.” Then Jacob knew that she had done a kindness to him by serving him as a wife.
verses.15: And he became a man before he could speak. Then, Rebekah came out; she was the daughter of Bethuel, the son of Nahor, Abraham’s brother. And she was pregnant with a child.
verses.16: And the young girl was very beautiful in her youth. No one knew who she was. Then the night fell, and darkness covered everything.
verses.17: And the servant ran to call for water. He said, “Please give me some water from there.”
verses.18: And she said, “Come here, Adonai!” Then she rushed forward and stepped onto it. She then kissed it.
verses.19: And she tried to comfort him. She said, “Even if you’re all gone, I will still stay here.”
verses.20: And she rushed forward, towards the well. She ran again towards the river to fetch water for all her needs.
verses.21: And the man must ask her to help him determine whether Jehovah will be satisfied with his ways or not.
verses.22: And when the gold rings were finished, the man took out a golden ring from its cavity. There were also two pendants on his hands, each weighing ten ounces of gold.
verses.23: And the daughter of Mi said, “Please tell me whether there is a place in your father’s house where we can live.”
verses.24: And the daughter of Bithuel said to him, “I am the daughter of a king who was born to Nahor.”
verses.25: And they said to him, “Also, there is a place for the wood and the spices with us. There’s also room for the lambs.”
verses.26: And the man bowed down and worshiped Yahweh.
verses.27: And blessed be Jehovah, the God of Abraham, who did not abandon his kindness and truth along with my Lord. I will rest in the path of Jehovah’s house.
verses.28: And the young man ran away and told his mother about all these things.
verses.29: And Lervaka’s brother, whose name was Laban, rushed towards the man who was in the valley.
verses.30: And he saw the flames and the smoke, as his brother handled them. When he heard what Rebekah said, his brother said to him, “These are the words of the man who spoke to me.” Then he went to see that man. And there he saw him standing on the hilltop.
verses.31: And he said, “Blessed be Jehovah! Why do you stand outside? I have entered the house; there is room for those who need shelter.”
verses.32: And the man entered the house. He opened the curtains, and he gave them straw and food to eat. He also provided water for their feet and those of the people who were with him.
verses.33: And he set food before him. But he said, “I will not eat until I hear what I have to say.” And the other person said, “Speak.”
verses.34: And the servant of Abraham said, “I am it.”
verses.35: And Jehovah blessed Adonai greatly. He exalted him, and gave him sheep, cattle, silver, gold, servants, women, and horses.
verses.36: And Sarai, the wife of Adam, gave birth to a son for Adam after her old age. And he gave him everything he owned.
verses.37: And Adonai said to me, “Do not take any wife from the daughters of the Canaanites, who live in their land.”
verses.38: If not to my father’s house, then go to my family and take a wife for my son.
verses.39: And he said to his master, “Do not let the woman go after me.”
verses.40: And the LORD said to me, “I will send a malefactor after you. He will hinder your path and make it difficult for you to proceed with your plans. You will also take a wife from my family and from my father’s house.”
verses.41: Then I will be cleansed from my sin, if you go to my family. But if they don’t give you permission, then you will remain unclean from my sin.
verses.42: And today, I come before the throne. I say, “Lord, God of Abraham, if it is possible, please help me along my path.”
verses.43: Now, I stand on the shore of the sea. It was a beautiful day when I arrived there. I said to her, “Please give me some water from your waters.”
verses.44: And she said to me, “You too must do this. And for your clothes, I will provide them.” She was the woman who would bear the son of Adonai.
verses.45: I still haven’t eaten anything yet. I want to talk to my heart. Then, Ribka comes out. She sits down on the chair. The tears flow down from her eyes. I say to her, “Please, be kind to me.”
verses.46: She rushed down from her place, and said, “Put on your clothes. I will also wash your clothes.” And she washed both her clothes and those of the others.
verses.47: And I asked her, “Who are you?” She replied, “I am the daughter of Nebuchadnezzar, who had a king as son.” Then I put the incense on her lips, and the incense also was placed on her hands.
verses.48: And I will bow down and worship Jehovah. I will bless Jehovah, the God of Abraham, who has led me on the true path to take my brother’s daughter for me.
verses.49: And now, if they are indeed doing kindness and truth in their actions, then tell me. But if not, then I will curse them on their right hand or on their head.
verses.50: And Laban and Betuel said, “From Jehovah’s mouth it came forth. Whatever He says to you, whether good or bad, must be obeyed.”
verses.51: Look, Rebekah is before you. Go and be her wife to your son, as the LORD has said.
verses.52: And when Abraham’s servant heard their words, he bowed down to Jehovah on the ground.
verses.53: And the servant brought out all the silver and gold items, as well as clothes. He gave some of them to Rebekah, and from the rest, he gave some to his sister and mother.
verses.54: They ate and drank, along with the men who were with him. Then they lay down and slept. In the morning, they said, “Send me to Adonai.”
verses.55: And Ahia said to her, “Your mother shall keep the young man with us for twenty days, after which he must leave.”
verses.56: And he said to them, “Do not follow me. May Jehovah make my path successful. Then I will go to Adonai.”
verses.57: And they said, “Call the young girl and ask her.”
verses.58: And they called for Rebekah, and said to her, “Go with this man.” She replied, “I will go.”
verses.59: And they sent Rebekah, one of their women, along with her maid and the servant of Abraham, as well as his men.
verses.60: And they blessed Rebekah, and said to her, “You will become the mother of many children, and your descendants will inherit the land of Canaan.”
verses.61: And Rebekah and her daughters got up, mounted their camels, and followed the man. The servant took Rebekah with him and went along.
verses.62: And Isaac came from his mother’s womb. He lived in the land of Canaan.
verses.63: And Isaac went out into the field to spend the evening. He looked around, and he saw that there were camels arriving.
verses.64: And Rebekah raised her eyes and saw Isaac. Then she fell down from the loft.
verses.65: And she said to the servant, “Who is this man who goes into the field to call upon us?” The servant replied, “He’s my master.” Then she took off her veil and went inside.
verses.66: And the servant told Isaac all the things that he had done.
verses.67: And Isaac brought his wife Rebekah to the camp. He took Rebekah as his wife, and he loved her. Isaac comforted his mother because of her.
